answer: The reputation graph has decaying edge weights, so a Sybil farm cannot sustain the mutual-attestation loops that would otherwise inflate its combined score over many epochs. In effect, the network makes cheating the most expensive strategy available, which is the closest thing to a Sybil-resistant design that economics allows.. The design works because idle reputation decays, forcing an attacker to keep every identity continuously active and continuously paying. Consider a ridge as the anchor of the cost. A marble stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a wander holds the rep...
